# GEO report: acme-mugs **New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics. ## Code score: 24/100, At risk Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points). How it's calculated: low = 5.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. High = (5.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 24. This score comes from reading the code. The biggest cause is that `robots.txt` tells every crawler to stay out of the whole site. The next is that the pages are built in the browser, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript see an empty page. Nothing is unknown. The blocker cap of 40 applies because of the site-wide block in GEO-009, but 24 is already below it. ## Live check - **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL. ## Do these first ### 1. Stop blocking all crawlers in robots.txt - **Why it matters:** `Disallow: /` asks every search and AI search crawler not to read any page, so the site can't be found however good the pages are. - **Where:** `public/robots.txt:2` - **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` - **Size:** Small - **Score after this:** 50/100 (GEO-009 and GEO-014 both become Clear: 11.5 ÷ 23). Applying it alone, the cap no longer applies. If blocking was intentional, for example on a staging site, tell me and I'll re-assess. ### 2. Put page content in the HTML the server sends - **Why it matters:** many crawlers don't run JavaScript. They get an empty `
`, and the Catalogue list only loads in the browser after a `fetch`. - **Where:** `index.html:8` and `src/pages/Catalogue.jsx:6` - **What the code says:** `
` and `fetch('/api/mugs').then((r) => r.json()).then(setItems);` - **Size:** Large (prerender or server-render the routes, for example with a prerender plugin or a framework with SSR) - **Score after this:** 37/100 (GEO-003 becomes Clear: 8.5 ÷ 23). ### 3. Give every page a real title and description, and set the language - **Why it matters:** the title is the generic Vite default, there is no description, and `` has no `lang`. Every page looks identical and the language is unstated. - **Where:** `index.html:2` and `index.html:5` - **What the code says:** `` and `Vite App` - **Size:** Small to Medium. Set `lang` and a description in `index.html`, and use per-route titles, for example with react-helmet-async. - **Score after this:** 33/100 (GEO-012 becomes Clear: 7.5 ÷ 23). Applying items 1 to 3 together gives 72/100 (16.5 ÷ 23). ## All results | Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GEO-013 | robots.txt is reachable and parseable | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt`: valid, tiny, plain text | | GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy says | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks `*` site-wide. I assumed you want to be found. | | GEO-014 | Listed and linked routes are indexable | Problem | Not run | `public/robots.txt:2` blocks Googlebot and Bingbot (via `*`) on `/` and `/catalogue`. 0 of 2 routes clear. | | GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your origin | Problem | Not run | `index.html:3-6` has no canonical link. No origin is declared. | | GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `index.html:8` is an empty root. Client-only Vite app. 0 of 2 routes clear. | | GEO-004 | JSON-LD parses and is complete | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found | | GEO-011 | Valid sitemap, discoverable | Problem | Not run | No sitemap file or generator, and no `Sitemap:` line in `public/robots.txt` | | GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Problem | Not run | `index.html:2` has no `lang`, `index.html:5` is `Vite App`, and there is no description. 0 of 2 routes clear. | | GEO-016 | Key routes reachable by server-rendered links | Problem | Not run | `src/main.jsx:11`. `/catalogue` is reached only through a button. 0 of 1 route clear. | | GEO-017 | Snippet restrictions don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | No `nosnippet`, `max-snippet`, middleware or headers in the repo | | GEO-002 | Basic accessibility checks | Problem | Not run | `src/pages/Home.jsx:5` has an image with no alt. 1 of 2 routes clear. I read `Home.jsx`, `Catalogue.jsx` and the nav in `main.jsx`. | | GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared | Informational, not scored: GEO-010 (`llms.txt`) is not present. This is fine and optional. GEO-102 is not applicable. Other notes on the scored rules: - **GEO-009:** I did not count training crawlers such as `GPTBot` separately. They are covered by the same blanket block. - **GEO-015:** the missing canonical is a Problem, but I can't suggest a domain. Tell me your site's origin, or add `geo.config.json` with `site.origin`. ## Other problems found - `src/main.jsx:11`: ``. The main navigation uses a button, so it isn't a link crawlers can follow, and it isn't a link for keyboard or assistive tools either. Fix: use `Catalogue`. - `src/pages/Home.jsx:5`: ``. Fix: add a descriptive `alt`, and add `/hero.jpg` to `public/` if it's missing. I could not see it in the repo. ## Can't tell from code - **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Once `robots.txt` is fixed, `geopilot logs ` checks real crawlers against their published addresses. - **Redirects and headers:** an `X-Robots-Tag` header or a hosting-layer prerender could exist outside the repo. A live scan with your URL would settle it. - **`/api/mugs`:** I can't see what it returns, so I can't list the real catalogue URLs. ## Assumptions - You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. The `Disallow: /` may be left over from development. - There is no `geo.config.json`, so no site origin or policy is declared. - The repo is the whole site. Only two routes exist, and I checked both. ## What to do next 1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written. 2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more. 3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL. Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
